convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
Jorge has an edge today — something curdled.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret. Just... be straight with me."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"Now then — I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held."
"Still on what you believe in."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Choir Toad? Patricia is pushing 'The Loud Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I should get back to it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
They nod. "Okay."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my niece, Maya. Is napping in a pod somewhere, they say. Seven years old and napping. She was never boring. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Told you."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"The whole fire was arguing about Choir Toad last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.'"
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I count meals, not days. Three meals since the rain. Two since the alarm. Days are for people with calendars. I have a stomach."
"Still on what day it is. That's the priority."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling Static? Patricia is pushing 'Ugly-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.' No rush."
"My part? I rinse the cup twice and stay ready."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you count the days — someone has to. What's the count today? Still keeping it?"
"Thank you. I wanted to check."
"Watch for this: It goes perfectly still and arches its back to the sun. Sunback, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." Back before, I was nobody special. This is my chance to be someone who matters.
"Just... if you see me do something well, say so. I know how that sounds. I don't care."
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never did finish talking about what was on their mind — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Still nothing on Maya. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Stan — The Pit, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening, anyway."
You show them Egusi Melon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you believe we get through this — the alternative doesn't work. Still holding the line?"
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Okay, but what about Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Ava owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? At night I cry quietly so no one hears."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration. I won't forget that."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Bessie sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said the most useful thing you learned is being hungry and going anyway. Still the lesson?"
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"I eat fast and leave early. Not hiding. Just — scheduling."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
